# The College Football Stability System — pp. 40–44

> **Source class: GUIDE CONTENT.** Every record, percentage, span and threshold below is printed in the 2026 VSiN College Football Betting Guide and is reproduced as printed. **Nothing here is backtested, recomputed, extended or projected** — this library holds no game-level historical data and does not manufacture any. Grouping trends into angles, and any check of a printed record against its printed percentage, are **TTW DERIVED** and labelled where they appear.

*Steve Makinen.* The guide's only fully specified betting system, and the one it supplies the most historical evidence for.

## The revised system is two rules, each with its own record

Makinen calls this his *official new College Football Stability System(s)* — plural. Both rules apply to non-conference games in the first four weeks, and both exclude games with a point spread of -30 or higher for either team.

| Rule | Condition | Record as printed | ATS % | Span |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **PLAY ON** | Play ON any team with a STABILITY SCORE EDGE of 6+ in non-conference games in the first four weeks (Weeks 0-3), assuming the game does NOT have a point spread of -30 or higher for either team. | 335-222 SU, 302-243-12 ATS | 55.4% | since 2013 |
| **FADE** | Play AGAINST any team with STABILITY SCORES of 0-6 in non-conference games in the first four weeks (Weeks 0-3) versus teams with higher scores, assuming the game does NOT have a point spread of -30 or higher for either team. | 259-136 SU, 217-173-4 ATS | 55.6% | since 2013 |

## What happened in 2025, in the guide's own account

30-36 ATS. Makinen reports this as a failure, not a footnote. He had flagged before the 2025 season that programme stability was changing because of the transfer portal, but ran the methodology as-is because the system had suffered only one losing season since 2013. He says it backfired, and that he promised to dig into the nuts and bolts to see whether what he was doing still made sense in this new era.

## What he changed

He reports three findings from that review: conference games were pulling the winning percentage down — teams with an old stability edge of seven points or more in conference games were winning only around 49.5% ATS; games with point spreads of 30 or more were hurting results; and the treatment of certain teams needed revisiting. The revised rule he states is to play against any team with a Stability Score of 0–6 in non-conference games in the first four weeks versus teams with higher scores.

## The premise

Teams in more stable year-to-year situations are better bets early, while teams that have undergone significant offseason change should be faded. Makinen calls the logic fundamentally sound: returning fewer starters, starting over at quarterback, and welcoming new head coaches or coordinators are all hurdles.

**Window.** The first four weeks of every season — Weeks 0, 1, 2 and 3.

**Scope.** The component trends include FBS vs. FBS games only. The system covers Weeks 0–3 and makes no claim about the rest of the season.

**Transfer quarterbacks.** Makinen counts a transfer quarterback as a NEW quarterback even with three years of starting experience elsewhere, because he is still learning new schemes. He allows there are degrees to this.
